source.title: Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m

record.tranche_reason: The study compares independently trained models using different measures from grokking studies, including cross-seed component-effect prediction and functional feature transfer. These results bear on whether runs learn the same identifiable algorithm, but do not test grokking training trajectories.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions grokking as related work but does not report training-accuracy saturation, delayed test-accuracy improvement, training-set-size effects, or the other grokking claims. The included results bear on V6: whether independently trained models on the same task have the same identifiable algorithm. The behavioral KL results are not included as rows because behavior alone does not measure algorithm identity.
record.test_reason: Not a grokking study. On a small algorithmic task (bounded-depth Dyck-3), it compares independently seeded runs. It tests whether they share an identifiable mechanism: behaviour, parameters under symmetry alignment, component-effect transfer, and SAE feature transfer with and without rotation. That bears on V6 in a new task setting. The Pythia-70m language-model results measure representational similarity, not an identifiable algorithm, so they fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that same-architecture runs compute the same function in residual-stream bases differing by an essentially Haar-random rotation ('polymorphism'), and that one Procrustes fit largely restores SAE and steering transfer. They also say parameter-level alignment and component-effect predictions fail across seeds and some non-rotational residual remains. Frontier-scale testing is left open.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes cross-seed mechanistic and activation-space alignment, SAE transfer, and component effects; it does not reproduce grokking's training-trajectory and delayed-generalization measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation-space transfer changes substantially when a Procrustes rotation is applied; the final Pythia residual site has lower decoder matching than intermediate sites. Shared versus independent I/O changes parameter-level alignment, while the authors report activation-level rotation recovery in both settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Across nine Pythia-70m seeds, residual-stream bases differ by a Haar-random rotation. Naive SAE transfer has negative EV, post-rotation EV is 0.85–0.99, and post-rotation firing correlations are 0.25–0.44.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained language models share features up to a residual-stream rotation (representational universality modulo rotation).

record.code_released: The paper says a supplementary code archive is provided; URL not stated.
record.problems: Evidence concerns cross-seed representation and component-effect alignment, not grokking. The within-seed causal/predictive bars are described as tautological or sanity checks; cross-seed Bar Pr collapses to Bar C in the implementation. Some aggregate results are reported as ranges across sites or pairs rather than individual values. The study does not test architectures or hyperparameters against one another.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other rotation, steering, checkpoint-drift, and parameter-alignment results because they do not directly measure whether independently trained runs use the same identifiable algorithm. No grokking trajectory findings were reported. See Sections 3–9.

untested.parts: No variation of architecture or hyperparameters (all runs share architecture and recipe; only seeds differ). No grokking or modular-arithmetic setting. No test of whether runs pick distinct named algorithms (e.g. clock vs pizza).
No train/test accuracy trajectories, delay, or training-set-size effects.
No progress measures or circuit formation over training.
No initialization-scale or weight-norm switch of delayed generalization.
No delayed generalization in LLM training (the Pythia checkpoint comparison concerns basis drift only).
No critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No optimizer or floating-point artifact test.

missing.what: Cohort B (fully independent-init Dyck-3 seeds 100–104): naive EV −1.53 to −0.58, post-rotation EV 0.965–0.987, Bar P max MSE 6.8–8.6, Bar B passes 3/4 pairs. This is the only fully independent-run test of V6.

Cross-seed Bar P after symmetry alignment: max MSE 0.490–0.580 baseline, 0.264–0.298 after Cayley refinement; joint weight/activation optimisation never clears threshold. These are parameter-level mechanism differences beyond the symmetry group.
Cross-seed Bar B (behavioural KL): passes for pairs 0v1, 0v3, 0v4; near-miss for 0v2 (1.90e-4). Behaviour is the same across seeds.

record.verdict_notes: The study never mentions grokking except as related work (citing Nanda et al. 2023). The V6 link rests only on the Dyck-3 toy; Cohort A shares frozen I/O weights, which makes the runs partially coordinated. The claim's architecture/hyperparameter axis is untouched. R5–R8 duplicate R1–R4 by the authors' own statement. The reader's rows_left_out excluded the parameter-alignment results as not bearing on algorithm identity; they do bear on it and should be rows.

versions.untested_parts: No training-accuracy or test-accuracy trajectory, overfitting delay, or training-set-size comparison.
No measurement of gradual generalizing-circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, or progress measures anticipating a test-accuracy jump.
No grokking-like delay on non-algorithmic data or test of initialization scale or weight norm as a switch for such delays.
No delayed generalization during realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No test of a low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.

Tests different random seeds on the same task and architecture, including Pythia-70m. Does not compare architectures or hyperparameters, and does not establish that every run converges to one identical, uniquely identified algorithm.
No test of adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts as an explanation for grokking delays.

relationships.condition: Dyck-3 seeds, activation level after one Procrustes rotation (shared-I/O cohort; independent-init cohort per text)
relationships.reason: Post-rotation SAE reconstruction is within 0.025 EV of self at every site, and decoder features match at ≥98% (R10, R17). Text reports the same for independent-init Cohort B (EV 0.965–0.987). Cross-seed behaviour matches (Bar B passes 3/4).
relationships.display_finding: After rotation, SAE reconstruction stayed within 0.025 explained variance of self-reconstruction at every site and decoder features matched at ≥98%; independently initialized models reached 0.965–0.987 explained variance, and three of four behavioral checks passed.

relation.reason: The study directly tests cross-seed mechanistic universality through aligned component effects, feature firing, and representation transfer, bearing on V6.

tranche.reason: Sections 7–9 provide results and an explicit refinement of universality: activation-level transfer improves under rotation while component-effect transfer and feature firing remain incomplete. This qualifies V6 rather than simply extending it to a new setting.

source_check.notes: Cross-seed Bars C and Pr duplicate one measurement over 10 components. Cohort A shares frozen I/O; Procrustes fits are site-specific. The study does not measure grokking's delayed-generalization trajectory.
